title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, billing qualifications and documented control paths are supported. Both API calls match Microsoft's documentation, including the allocation request body and the consumption endpoint's deprecation. The testing and evaluation checklist step has no corresponding controls-table row, a minor consistency issue.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow creates an inline agent whose instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape are configured in the node and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote:

No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment allocation controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, including agents, workflows and prompts, rather than only agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.claim: Tenant-pool draw is selected by default for eligible Copilot Studio environments without an allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: An environment-group rule makes the environment's tenant-draw setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic allocation requests cannot override an environment-group rule governing tenant draw.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio shows Agent flow actions used by each workflow.
claims.quote: In the [Power Platform admin center](https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com/) > **Licensing** > **Copilot Studio**, review the **Agent flow actions** used by each workflow.

claims.claim: The printed GET environment resource consumption call uses the documented method, path, required dates and API version, with MCSMessages as the Copilot Credits entitlement.
claims.quote: GET https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/entitlements/{entitlementId}/environments/{environmentId}/resources?fromDate={fromDate}&toDate={toDate}&api-version=2024-10-01

claims.quote: Get environment resource entitlement snapshots for an entitlement (deprecated).

claims.quote: Searched: get-environment-resources reference for workflow-level guarantees. Opened and read the complete reference, including EnvironmentResourceEntitlementSnapshotResponseModel; it documents resourceId, consumed and metadata, not a workflow-level breakdown guarantee.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column reporting each workflow's consumption.
claims.quote: The **Credit usage (last 30 days)** column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.

claims.claim: Workflows already running complete normally when prepaid capacity is consumed.

claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "monthly" "limit". Opened agent-node-workflow and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness; read capacity-management search excerpts. Agent limits are documented, but no inline-node credit cap is stated.
